extracted.intended_audience: State of Maine agencies and stakeholders (rulemaking staff, agency attorneys, and members of the public interested in Maine rulemaking)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the Maine Administrative Procedure Act (MAPA) requirements and resources that govern how State of Maine agencies must propose, adopt, publish, and have their administrative actions reviewed. Focused on procedural compliance and public notice for state agency rulemaking and related administrative actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: MAPA governs state agency rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: The Maine Administrative Procedure Act ("MAPA") governs rulemaking conducted by State of Maine agencies and is codified in Title 5 of the Maine Revised Statutes at sections 8001 through 11116.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must follow the MAPA process when they propose and adopt rules they are to administer and enforce. The Act was first enacted in 1977 and has been amended multiple times; it has been affected by Executive Order 4 (3/4/2019). Contact the Secretary of State's office for assistance or questions about Maine's online rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: MAPA provides uniform, comprehensive procedures for administrative actions
rubrics_metrics.description: MAPA establishes a uniform, comprehensive set of procedures covering the administrative actions of state agencies, including rulemaking, advisory rulings, adjudicatory proceedings, and licensing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirements under MAPA apply across these categories of agency activity; agencies should treat rulemaking, advisory rulings, adjudications, and licensing consistently with MAPA's procedural framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: MAPA establishes judicial review of agency actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act covers judicial review of those actions (agency administrative actions governed by MAPA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency actions taken under MAPA are subject to judicial review according to the standards and procedures set out in the statute; agencies should be mindful that procedural compliance affects reviewability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain public notice, publication, and electronic notification resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of State provides quick-reference links such as Weekly Rulemaking Notices, Adopted State of Maine Agency Rules, a Directory of Agency Rulemaking Liaisons, and a link to the Maine Legislature's 'Electronic Notification of Agency Rulemaking Application' webpage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These resources facilitate transparency and public access to rulemaking. Agencies are expected to use available publication and electronic-notification mechanisms (and the public/stakeholders should monitor them) to ensure timely notice and availability of proposed and adopted rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: MAPA may be modified or informed by executive actions
rubrics_metrics.description: MAPA 'has been affected by Executive Order 4 (3/4/2019).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive orders or other statewide directives can modify how MAPA is implemented in practice; agencies should watch for executive actions that affect MAPA procedures and adjust compliance practices accordingly.
